slides.heading: Merge Binary Trees
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Binary Trees
slides.narration: Let's solve Merge Binary Trees, a medium binary trees problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Overlay two trees; overlapping nodes sum their values.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Overlay two trees; overlapping nodes sum their values. Mutates and returns tree1.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Overlay the trees node by node: add values where both exist, otherwise keep whichever exists.
slides.narration: Overlay the trees node by node: add values where both exist, otherwise keep whichever exists.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Build a brand-new tree → O(n + m) extra space
Merge into tree 1 in place → O(min(n, m)) time
Reuse subtrees where only one side exists
slides.narration: Building a new tree copies everything. Merging into the first tree in place is cheaper: we only recurse where both trees have nodes, and reuse a subtree whenever one side is missing.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. If one tree is null, return the other
3. Merge left children and right children
slides.narration: Step by step. First, if one tree is null, return the other. Second, add the values. Third, merge left children and right children.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Two trees to overlay
slides.narration: We overlay two trees: where both have a node, add the values; otherwise keep whichever exists.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Overlapping nodes summed
slides.narration: Root one plus one gives two; three plus five gives eight; two plus nine gives eleven; seven plus two gives nine.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Missing on one side → reuse the other subtree
slides.narration: Where only one tree has a node, like four from tree one, or seven and six from tree two, we simply reuse that subtree.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: If either tree is null, return the other. Otherwise add the second value into the first, merge the left children, merge the right children, and return the first tree.

slides.heading: Complexity
bullets: Time: O(n) of the smaller overlap
slides.narration: Time is O of n of the smaller overlap. Space is O of h.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: Handle either tree being null, and mention that the result mutates and shares structure with the inputs.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Ask if inputs may be modified
Iterative with a stack of pairs
slides.narration: Ask whether modifying the inputs is acceptable; otherwise build new nodes.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Overlay the trees node by node: add values where both exist, otherwise keep whichever exists.
Complexity: O(n) of the smaller overlap
